Note::unquote¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::unquote() const

Strip One Matching Pair Of Surrounding Quotes¶

unquote() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with one matching pair of surrounding quote characters removed from each cell. It is the inverse of quote and the cleanup step for values that arrive pre-quoted — a CSV field, a shell argument, a config string.

A cell is unquoted only when both its first and last characters are the same quote character — either "..." or '...'. Then exactly those two characters are removed and nothing else: no unescaping, no interior processing, no repeated stripping. If the ends do not match (only one side quoted, or the two ends are different quote characters, or the cell is unquoted already), the cell is returned unchanged.

Because neither quote() nor unquote() escapes, quote().unquote() round-trips exactly, and unquote() on a cell whose content itself contains quotes strips only the outermost pair — see Example 2.

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. "" (two quote characters) unquotes to the empty string.

Example 1: Double And Single Quotes¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"\"double\"", "'single'", "bare"}).unquote())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["double", "single", "bare"]

"bare" has no surrounding quotes and is unchanged.

Example 2: Only A Matching Pair Is Removed¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::make_note(
    {"\"unbalanced", "trailing\"", "\"\"", "\"a\"b\""}).unquote();
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["\"unbalanced", "trailing\"", "", "a\"b"]

Cells 0 and 1 are quoted on one side only and are left as-is. "" unquotes to empty. "a"b" has matching " at both ends, so those two are removed, leaving the interior a"b.

Example 3: Round-Trip With quote¶

pluss::note::print(std::cout,
                   pluss::make_note({"payload", "  spaced  "}).quote().unquote())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["payload", "  spaced  "]

The boundary spaces survive because quote/unquote touch only the outermost characters.

Example 4: A Scalar¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::make_note("\"solo\"").unquote()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"solo"

See Also¶

  • Note::quote: the inverse — wrap each cell in "...".

  • Note::strip: strip("\"'") removes runs of quote characters from both ends, not just one matching pair.

  • pluss::coden::Note::remove_prefix / remove_suffix: remove a specific known delimiter from one end.
